builtWith.heading: How This Page Was Built

body.t: One content file holds every line of this resume in two registers with a source for each claim. Three builds read it: this page, a Word copy for applicant tracking systems, and the two PDFs printed from this page. Before anything is published, I run a scan script on it that flags em-dashes, a list of filler phrases, and any client name. Built in Claude Code sessions under those rules, the same way I run client work: write the rules down, let the tooling enforce them, keep one source of truth.
body.p: Everything on this page comes from one file that holds each line twice, once in plain words and once in Salesforce terms, with a note on where each claim comes from. Three things are built from that file: this page, a Word copy for job-application systems, and the two PDFs. Before anything is published, I run a checking script on it that catches any em-dash, filler phrase, or client name. Built with Claude Code, the same way I run client work: write the rules down, let the tools enforce them, keep one source of truth.

title.p: What a test-system reset would break

what.t: Lists everything a sandbox refresh wipes or breaks (scheduled jobs, OAuth tokens, credentials, sites, custom settings, recent setup changes) with an owner column, wrapped in a Claude Code skill that asks first and drafts the client note.
what.p: Before a test copy of Salesforce gets wiped and rebuilt, it lists everything that will be lost or broken, so each item gets an owner instead of a surprise.

title.t: Adopting AI safely in a Salesforce shop
